# JSON results reference

<!-- Generated by tools/L3Lint.DocsGen from schemas/results.schema.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

This is the shape of `l3lint lint --output json`, the contract for machines. The MCP tool `lint_payload` returns the same transaction and finding objects. See [Output formats](../articles/output-formats.md) for the other formats and the exit codes.

Schema: [results.schema.json](../schemas/results.schema.json) (JSON Schema draft 2020-12, `$id` `https://brimatt16219.github.io/l3lint/schemas/results.schema.json`). `l3lint schema results` prints the same file.

The JSON output of l3lint lint. Findings are advisory: they say a payload is likely to downgrade or meets the documented requirement. Card networks and issuers decide the rate.

Types read "string or null" when a property may also be `null`. In the tables, an object that has its own table links to it.

<a id="schema-root"></a>

## Root object

| Property | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schemaVersion` | string | no | always `1.0` | Results schema version. |
| `tool` | object, see [tool](#schema-tool) | yes |  | The tool that wrote the results. |
| `rulePacks` | map of string keys to string | yes |  | Rule pack ID to pack version. |
| `asOf` | string or null | no | pattern `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$` | The --as-of date when given, else null (each transaction then carries its own as-of date). |
| `profile` | string | no |  | Processor profile used. |
| `inputs` | array of object, see [inputs[]](#schema-inputs) | yes |  | Every input of the run, in the order given. |
| `inputErrors` | array of object, see [inputErrors[]](#schema-inputerrors) | no |  | Inputs, or NDJSON records, that could not be read. Each one makes the exit code at least 2. |
| `transactions` | array of [transaction](#schema-transaction) | yes |  | One entry per transaction, in input order. |
| `batchFindings` | array of [finding](#schema-finding) | no |  | Findings about the run as a whole, such as GEN-DQ-007. Each points at the first transaction that carries the repeated value. |
| `summary` | object, see [summary](#schema-summary) | yes |  | Counts over every finding, including findings left out by --max-findings. |
| `notes` | array of string | no |  | Notes about the run, such as where the settings came from. |
| `exitCode` | integer | yes | at least 0; at most 3 | The exit code of the run: 0 clean or below --fail-on, 1 findings at or above --fail-on, 2 usage or input error, 3 rule pack, config or internal error. |

No other properties are allowed.

<a id="schema-tool"></a>

## tool

The tool that wrote the results.

| Property | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | yes |  | Always l3lint. |
| `version` | string | yes |  | Engine version, for example 1.0.0. |
| `informationUri` | string | no |  | Project home page. |

No other properties are allowed.

<a id="schema-inputs"></a>

## inputs[]

| Property | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | yes |  | The path as given (relative paths stay relative), or - for standard input. |
| `format` | string | yes |  | The format the input was read as, for example stripe; unknown when it could not be read. |
| `sha256` | string | yes | at least 1 character | Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the input's bytes. |
| `transactions` | integer | yes | at least 0 | How many transactions the input held. |

No other properties are allowed.

<a id="schema-inputerrors"></a>

## inputErrors[]

| Property | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | yes |  | The input that failed. |
| `line` | integer or null | no |  | The line where reading failed, when known. |
| `message` | string | yes |  | What went wrong and what to change. |
| `candidates` | array of string | no |  | The formats that tied when detection could not choose; pass one with --format. |

No other properties are allowed.

<a id="schema-summary"></a>

## summary

Counts over every finding, including findings left out by --max-findings.

| Property | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `transactions` | integer | yes | at least 0 | Transactions linted. |
| `errors` | integer | yes | at least 0 | Error findings. |
| `warnings` | integer | yes | at least 0 | Warning findings. |
| `information` | integer | yes | at least 0 | Information findings. |
| `byRule` | map of string keys to integer | yes | values: at least 0 | Rule ID to the number of findings it raised. |
| `byBrand` | map of string keys to object, see [summary.byBrand.*](#schema-summary-bybrand) | no |  | Brand to finding counts. A general rule's findings count under the transaction's brand. |
| `findingsShown` | integer | no | at least 0 | Findings written to the output. Present only when --max-findings left some out. |
| `findingsOmitted` | integer | no | at least 0 | Findings left out by --max-findings. Present only when above 0. |

No other properties are allowed.

<a id="schema-summary-bybrand"></a>

## summary.byBrand.*

| Property | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `errors` | integer | yes | at least 0 | Error findings for the brand. |
| `warnings` | integer | yes | at least 0 | Warning findings for the brand. |
| `information` | integer | yes | at least 0 | Information findings for the brand. |

No other properties are allowed.

<a id="schema-transaction"></a>

## transaction

The result for one transaction.

| Property | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `index` | integer | yes | at least 0 | 0-based position of the transaction in the run. |
| `input` | integer | yes | at least 0 | 0-based index of its input in inputs. |
| `id` | string or null | no |  | The transaction ID from the payload. |
| `brand` | string | no | one of `visa`, `mastercard`, `amex`, `discover`, `unknown` | The effective card brand: the --brand flag, else the payload, else the config file. |
| `brands` | array of string | no | items: one of `visa`, `mastercard`, `amex`, `discover`, `unknown` | Every brand evaluated: one brand normally, all four with --brand all. Absent when the brand is unknown and only general rules ran. |
| `cardProduct` | string or null | no | one of `consumer`, `business`, `corporate`, `purchasing`, `fleet`, `commercialPrepaid`, `unknown` | The effective card product. |
| `mcc` | string or null | no |  | The effective merchant category code. |
| `format` | string | no |  | The adapter that read the transaction, for example stripe. |
| `asOf` | string or null | no | pattern `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$` | The date whose rules applied: --as-of, else transactionDate, else the day of the run. |
| `likelyTier` | [tier](#schema-tier) or null | no |  | The tier rollup for the transaction's brand, or null when the brand is unknown. |
| `likelyTiers` | array of [tier](#schema-tier) | no |  | One tier rollup per evaluated brand. Present when more than one brand was evaluated. |
| `costEstimate` | [costEstimate](#schema-costestimate) | no |  | Estimated cost from the user's rate table. Present only with --rates. |
| `notes` | array of string | no |  | Notes such as context overrides and adapter remarks. |
| `findings` | array of [finding](#schema-finding) | yes |  | The findings, sorted by canonical path, then rule ID. |

No other properties are allowed.

<a id="schema-finding"></a>

## finding

One rule result on one transaction.

| Property | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ruleId` | string | yes | pattern <code>^((GEN&#124;VISA&#124;MC&#124;AMEX&#124;DISC)-[A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]{3}&#124;L3LINT-[A-Z]+-[0-9]{3})$</code> | The rule ID, for example VISA-L3-004, or an engine diagnostic ID such as L3LINT-ENGINE-001. |
| `severity` | string | yes | one of `error`, `warning`, `information` | The effective severity after profile scoping and overrides. |
| `impact` | string | yes | one of `blocksLevel3`, `blocksLevel2`, `riskVisaValidation`, `truncation`, `noBenefit`, `hygiene` | What the finding means for the interchange tier. |
| `brand` | string | no | one of `visa`, `mastercard`, `amex`, `discover`, `unknown` | The brand whose pack raised the finding. Absent for general rules. |
| `transactionIndex` | integer | no | at least 0 | 0-based index of the transaction. Present in batchFindings. |
| `path` | object, see [finding.path](#schema-finding-path) | yes |  | Where the problem is. |
| `location` | object, see [finding.location](#schema-finding-location) or null | no |  | Line and column of the value in the input file, or null when the value is absent or the position is unknown. |
| `message` | string | yes |  | What is wrong, in plain words. |
| `expected` | string or null | no |  | What the rule expected, when it can be stated. |
| `actual` | string or null | no |  | The value found, already masked for card numbers; null when the value is absent. |
| `fix` | string | yes |  | How to fix it, stated as an action. |
| `patch` | array of [patchOperation](#schema-patchoperation) or null | no |  | A mechanical RFC 6902 patch for this finding, or null when there is none. |
| `needsHuman` | boolean | no |  | True when a person must decide the fix, for example a proposed unit mapping. Absent otherwise. |
| `confidence` | string | yes | one of `public-brand`, `processor-doc`, `inferred`, `policy` | The rule's confidence label. |
| `sources` | array of string | yes |  | Public pages the rule comes from. |

No other properties are allowed.

<a id="schema-finding-path"></a>

## finding.path

Where the problem is.

| Property | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `canonical` | string | yes |  | JSON Pointer in the canonical payload, for example /lineItems/1/commodityCode. |
| `source` | string or null | no |  | The same place in the original format, such as a Stripe JSON Pointer or a CSV cell label; null when the format has no such field. |

No other properties are allowed.

<a id="schema-finding-location"></a>

## finding.location

| Property | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `line` | integer | yes | at least 1 | 1-based line in the input file. |
| `column` | integer | yes | at least 1 | 1-based column in the input file. |

No other properties are allowed.

<a id="schema-tier"></a>

## tier

The tier rollup for one brand: the best tier the card and MCC allow and the tier the data likely reaches.

| Property | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `brand` | string | no | one of `visa`, `mastercard`, `amex`, `discover`, `unknown` | The brand. Present in likelyTiers entries. |
| `best` | string | yes | one of `product3`, `product2`, `belowProduct3`, `belowProduct2`, `dataRate3`, `dataRate2`, `dataRate1`, `none` | The best tier the card and MCC allow, or none. |
| `likely` | string | yes | one of `product3`, `product2`, `belowProduct3`, `belowProduct2`, `dataRate3`, `dataRate2`, `dataRate1`, `none` | The tier the payload likely reaches. |
| `status` | string | yes | one of `meets`, `atRisk`, `blocked`, `noBenefit` | meets: the payload meets the documented requirements of the best tier. atRisk: Visa may still reject the data after settlement. blocked: an error finding blocks the best tier. noBenefit: no enhanced-data rate exists for this card, brand or MCC. |
| `blockingErrors` | integer | no | at least 0 | How many error findings blocked tiers. |

No other properties are allowed.

<a id="schema-costestimate"></a>

## costEstimate

Estimated interchange cost from the user's rate table. Always an estimate, never the actual fee.

| Property | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | string | yes | always `estimate` | Always estimate. |
| `rateTable` | string | yes |  | The rate table's name. |
| `effective` | string | yes |  | The rate table's effective date. |
| `currency` | string | yes |  | Currency of the amounts. |
| `estimates` | array of object, see [costEstimate.estimates[]](#schema-costestimate-estimates) | yes |  | One entry per evaluated brand that has categories in the rate table. |

No other properties are allowed.

<a id="schema-costestimate-estimates"></a>

## costEstimate.estimates[]

| Property | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `brand` | string | yes | one of `visa`, `mastercard`, `amex`, `discover`, `unknown` | The brand. |
| `likelyTier` | string | yes |  | The rate table tier used for the likely outcome. |
| `likelyCost` | number or null | yes |  | Estimated cost at the likely tier, or null when the table has no matching category. |
| `bestTier` | string | yes |  | The rate table tier used for the best outcome. |
| `bestCost` | number or null | yes |  | Estimated cost at the best tier, or null when the table has no matching category. |
| `difference` | number or null | yes |  | Likely cost minus best cost, when both exist: what the downgrade likely costs. |

No other properties are allowed.

<a id="schema-patchoperation"></a>

## patchOperation

One RFC 6902 JSON Patch operation in the source format's paths and units.

| Property | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `op` | string | yes | one of `add`, `remove`, `replace`, `move`, `copy`, `test` | The operation. |
| `path` | string | yes |  | JSON Pointer of the target value in the source document. |
| `from` | string | no |  | JSON Pointer of the source value, for move and copy. |
| `value` | any JSON value | no |  | The value to add, replace or test. |
